author: Bobby Grayson
description:
Replacement text for README.md (I am not allowed to edit it).
Status paragraph, the counts that moved: TWELVE worked examples (add log store and logs live), twelve Gen files, 76 translator fixtures (55 expect ok, 21 expect error). Three of the twelve are now modules that were not written for this repository: elixir/real/table_registry.ex, elixir/real/log_store.ex and elixir/real/logs_live.ex, each byte-for-byte from its origin (Loom.Teams.TableRegistry, Ensemble.LogStore, EnsembleWeb.LogsLive), translated with no annotations and no edits.
Property table rows to add:
| Log store | the entry count never exceeds max_entries | 11,737, mutation-tested (counter bumped on both branches) |
| Logs live | message handling is append-only: what the view shows stays, in order, at the front of what it shows next | 809, mutation-tested (prepend instead of append) |
Layout rows to add:
| Leanactors/Examples/LogStore.lean | Ensemble.LogStore translated with no annotations: hand beh, beh_eq_gen, the bounded count-bound check and the runaway-counter mutant |
| Leanactors/Examples/LogsLive.lean | EnsembleWeb.LogsLive, the LiveView that shows what the store broadcasts: hand beh, beh_eq_gen, the append-only check and the prepend mutant |
Untyped mode paragraph, extend the reply sentence: ... and the reply type from every reply expression in the file when all are literal atoms or tagged tuples. When none of them is a literal there is no union to infer but the expressions may still have one type between them, so the file is rendered once with the replies left out, the type each has in its own clause is collected, and if there is exactly one the whole file is compiled again with it -- so a list-valued reply carries a List Term rather than collapsing to the opaque Term.
New paragraph, LiveView assigns: A LiveView socket is a struct with an assigns map and Phoenix imports assign/2,3, which updates it functionally, so a socket is modelled as exactly the record the state machinery already had: assign(s, :k, e) is the field update, s.assigns.k the field read, and a module whose callbacks bind the socket whole but write named assigns infers a record state over those keys, each field typed by the shape of the values written to it. Nothing else about LiveView is modelled. mount/3 is the lifecycle, so the initial state comes from the spawn site the way a GenServer state does when there is no init/1; handle_event/3 is driven by the browser channel rather than by the mailbox, so it is not a clause of beh -- and because that IS a transition the real process makes, the generated file names it in a header line of its own instead of filing it under the public API wrappers.
Readiness paragraph numbers: 55 candidate modules, 3 translatable, 747 blockers in 106 families.
NOTES round-8 bullet: Two more real files, and the honest part is what they do not model. The log store needed a reply type that no declaration gives you: the only reply is a list, so the translator now compiles the file twice, once to find out what the replies are and once to use it. The LiveView needed the socket, which turned out to be the record state we already had with an assigns hop in front of it -- 126 of the survey's blockers were two functions, assign/2 and assign/3. But a LiveView also has handle_event, which is a real transition of the real process and is not in the model, and the temptation was to let it sit quietly in the list of untranslated public API. It gets its own line in every generated file instead.
